state.task: Revise the .can draft files themselves to supply complete frontend layouts and smooth en/nl presentation. The governing priorities are adoption, economy of source tokens, unchanged business semantics, and a single canonical mechanism for each SaaS primitive. These sources are intended for AI authors rather than human authors. The earlier requirements revision calls for an implicit left sidebar that collapses, brand content above automatically derived page links, a lower account menu, and a settings dialog divided internally into sections. The solution must avoid app wrapper files, authored build manifests, additional catalog files, duplicated authentication/team schemas, and repeated business-operation contracts.
state.evidence: Across 42 draft files, the current source declares 83 pages, 114 forms, 86 tables and 115 lists; authored navigation and card/details grouping are absent. Of the pages, 80 could enter static navigation and three depend on context. App-specific arrangements and useful personal settings are now documented in 39 app requirements files. The present grammar already admits responsive cards, Collapse details, generated drawers for mutation forms, typed collections and filters, bindings to actions, and automatically generated HTMX regions. Personal preference schemas, tabs, split views driven by a selected row, selection for detail drawers, and initial filter values are missing. The localization inventory comprises 361 descriptions, 85 literal UI strings, 1288 model/contract fields belonging to their owners, 461 parameters of user operations, 184 such operations, and 338 enum values declared directly. A restricted caption vocabulary would match 376 fields and 123 parameters. Declaration totals are broader than the surfaces established to be displayed. Implementation currently consists of a syntax parser; there is no running renderer, resolver or BDD engine.
state.research: Markup and CSS building blocks are available from daisyUI Drawer, Modal and Tab, while WAI-ARIA's dialog and tabs guidance describes the required focus handling, keyboard interaction and selection behavior. Swapping HTMX error responses needs deliberate configuration. Reusing translated schema attributes is illustrated by Rails i18n. These references establish neither the proposed automatic CanLang captions nor a correct runtime implementation. Retain CanLang's existing canonical facilities: messages belonging to the source owner, typed ICU message descriptors, description references written #=, effect-free exports, and outbound formatting through format(message,locale=null). User-entered and stored business content continues to display without translation.
state.preferences: Each logical owner may declare a single unnamed preferences {fields} schema in Given. Allowed fields hold typed scalars, enums or nullable references to records for which access is authorized; every nonnullable field requires a constant initial value. Exclude arrays, files, secrets, action values, objects and nested schema definitions. Account, language, appearance and security controls remain shared implicit settings rather than repeated preference fields. The runtime persists these values only for the authenticated user who owns them, within the selected app and team context. It supplies their settings inputs together with save/reset, checks values both when saving and when consuming them, and checks access to referenced records again. Anonymous rendering takes the schema's defaults. Pure validation can use the existing require preferences: row... form. A preferences.field reference may influence Then rendering, an authorized UI read selection, or validation of preferences. It cannot determine business admission guards, state changes, persisted business fields, scheduling or authority. If reference access is revoked, the runtime safely disregards or clears that value and gives feedback. An extension field is valid only with an actual consumer in a view. Neither source-authored CRUD for preferences nor a business MCP tool is added. Persist an extension under (user,selected app,canonical owner,current team or none). When composition reaches an owner more than once, render its settings section once. The base account settings continue to be shared.
state.ui: Preserve current groups and the canonical form mechanism. A list/table gains display=split to show one selected row in an authorized pane, becoming a drawer on mobile without changing its row scope. For details, introduce display=drawer; the default Collapse form accepts open=boolean presentation expression, and enclosing bindings continue into either details form. Collections can declare defaults={filter=preferences.field}. Every default key must be an existing filter key, URL or control selections take precedence, null leaves the initial filter unrestricted, and current authorization is checked again. Introduce tabs with an optional selector tied to an enum preference. A bound tabs preferences.view declaration can stand alone: selected enum captions are derived and the selected value supplies existing UI reads. With a block, tab enum_case children map content to distinct exact enum cases. Tabs without a preference binding instead require suites headed by tab captions and remember selection only as transient presentation state. Business enum fields cannot be changed by tabs. Exclude drag/drop, chart primitives, arbitrary HTML, and additional polling or query helpers. Generate navigation from accessible static pages in declaration order, omitting dynamic detail routes. A page can exceptionally declare nav=none or order=int, and group=caption is optional only for a real grouping difference. Composed sources share one shell, and suppression of navigation links conveys no authorization. Eliminate authored nav/link trees so that navigation derived from pages, with its page-local exceptions, is the sole navigation mechanism. There are no nav declarations in the current corpus that need migration. Only Collapse details admits open; a drawer can be opened solely for its single selected or activated record. Choosing a bound tab immediately calls the canonical preference save with version checking. Save failures must be visible and must return selection to the accepted value, without adding a second writer. Each enum case must occur exactly once among the children of a bound tab block.
state.localization: Keep one source-owned messages table using the existing mechanism for each owner, with English as the source and Dutch as the other column. Allow a canonical for binding to list comma-separated owned targets, reusing a complete caption only when all targets have the same meaning; repeated targets and targets belonging elsewhere still fail. Additional binding targets are for package for the owner's caption, for preferences for its settings section, and its preference fields and enum cases. Supply standard verbs and boolean captions once through runtime, alongside a finite pinned vocabulary matching exact field/parameter identifiers and types. Machine identities stay fixed; neither identifier splitting nor translation inferred from English is permitted. The reviewed matches are name,title,description,body,subject,reason,notes,instructions,evidence,reference,phone,address:text; email:email; timezone:timezone; currency:currency; quantity,count:int/decimal; active,enabled,done:bool; amount,price,total:money; duration:duration; at,occurred,created_at,updated_at:datetime; due:date/datetime; revision:int; file:file. The location caption may default only on text or the precise shared Location symbol. A reference parameter whose identifier matches its model name except for initial-letter case receives that model's owning caption; a renamed meaning must have an authored binding. Enum meanings receive no inference other than bool. Explicit translations remain required for other exposed schema, operation and role captions, domain enum cases, layout wording and descriptions. Labels and the referenced pure localization assets travel with exported schemas. Fixed outbound notices become typed patterns formatted explicitly against the app default, whereas dynamic persisted notices retain their status as data. Register any human-text output path of a custom capability against its exact pinned signature; a field called message is insufficient evidence of such a sink. Fix the runtime operation-verb vocabulary to submit,cancel,assign,reopen,complete,publish,pause,resume,refresh.
state.alternatives: An unnamed preferences declaration introduces one reserved contextual form, derives its identity and avoids repeated names, at the cost of restricting each owner to one extension schema. Naming preference schemas allows several groups with explicit references, increasing tokens and the amount of state exposed. Using ordinary models owned by the user retains existing CRUD but requires copied schemas and account wiring and introduces another personal-settings route. A small reviewed caption vocabulary saves recurring bindings while requiring exact versioned rules and possible overrides where meanings differ. Requiring authored captions everywhere makes wording directly visible but reproduces common phrases. Inferring translations and captions from identifiers minimizes authored source yet leaves ambiguous meanings and unstable wording. Listing multiple targets in a for binding saves repetitions of complete messages and introduces validation of that list.

preference_shape.instructions: Select the personal-settings extension form that best satisfies the given source restrictions and runtime requirements.

criteria.unnamed: Declare a single preferences schema with an identity derived for its owner; use canonical runtime save/reset and restrict consumption to presentation, retaining the limit of one schema.
criteria.named: Allow explicitly named personal preference schemas and references under the same ownership and validation restrictions, with the resulting additional names and groups.
criteria.ordinary_model: Represent settings through regular models owned by the user, ordinary CRUD and settings bindings, requiring the authored schemas and account wiring.
criteria.unresolved: Leave the declaration form undecided when every candidate fails one or more stated constraints.

label_policy.instructions: Choose the caption policy that best balances reliable complete localization against repeated source in these drafts.

criteria.finite_defaults: Version-pin the specified exact name/type vocabulary and reuse of referenced-type captions; write domain-specific meanings and necessary overrides in source.
criteria.explicit_labels: Make each caption an explicit binding of its owner, even for common repeated wording, reusing whole messages where useful.
criteria.generic_inference: Normalize or infer arbitrary identifiers to produce captions and translations, accepting that domain meanings may be ambiguous.
criteria.unresolved: Postpone this policy choice when the alternatives cannot provide predictable localization coverage.

ui_boundary.instructions: Do these UI rules confine preferences, tab selection, initial filters and record-detail arrangements to presentation, while retaining the canonical operations and present record/field permissions?

criteria.true: The proposed rules maintain the stated separation and introduce no competing means of business mutation or authorization.
criteria.false: At least one proposed rule allows, or fails to resolve, an alternative route to business mutation or authorization.

grouped_labels.instructions: Can the canonical for mechanism coherently assign one complete caption meaning to multiple targets of its owner under typed source-owned localization and the prohibition on duplicate contracts?

criteria.true: The proposed target list preserves ownership, prevents duplication, shares an intact message meaning and keeps the canonical binding rules.
criteria.false: The target-list proposal violates those constraints or leaves a competing binding mechanism unresolved.
